body:
CURRENT MERGER PROCEDURE; no authority.
During procedural repairs follow the ONE current local temporary rule, termal-greg-no-repeated-confirmation-2026-10-29. Repository instructions and the executor's actual permissions govern validation and landing. History stays in prior revisions and task notes. Adapted from Architect3's quoted Engram r37 (#118/13887323); this is not a claim to have read that foreign memory locally.

1. CODER owns changes, focused/new checks, dependency guards and the required independent review pair. Resolve all in-scope Medium+ findings and obtain the required re-review. Each attempt needs its original complete structured result; missing/failed submission is unavailable, not clean. Eligible roots of the original review project read as themselves with delegationId + submissionAttempt + resultId, pinned on every page. No parent impersonation or extra consent; a read grants no child control, credit or landing authority.

2. CODER -> MERGER: ONE complete READY names scope/item, owner/root, Git base/tree, launcher-consistent staged/clean state, original review references/dispositions and native run results/counts/before-after fingerprints. Read required original results at their native references. No partial-package progress, repeated packet audits, duplicate exports, manual source hashes or hash manifests for identified native records. Transfer a required inaccessible result only once. Delivery repair alone needs no new review/test. Explicit item requirements still apply.

3. MERGER is non-authoring: claim/accept through supported routes and integrate onto actual current master, preserving already-landed work. Name the owned source root per claim before editing; it takes effect next turn. Assess dependencies and carry identity. Adopt valid author reviews with unchanged-contribution proof and clean-carry conditions; master movement alone needs no extra Merger pair. Return any conflict, changed package content, unproved carry or product/test/fixture/doc fix to its Coder. A review does not carry a gate or acceptance verdict. No whole-blob overwrite of another contribution.

4. Validate the exact final input through the standard launcher and current repository requirements. Reuse only an applicable complete PASS on identical final input. Preserve native run id, terminal exit/outcome, required stage results/counts and automatic before/after input check. Failed/unrun is not PASS; absent result is UNKNOWN. Diagnose bounded failures, return defects to owner, recover existing results rather than rerun for delivery. No automatic repair/retry/reviewer loop or timeout weakening. Git identity follows termal-verification-by-git-not-manual-hashes; the actual launcher's clean/staged result governs. Equal commit/tree or stable fingerprint cannot override dirty exact-ref input. Remote rules: remote-test-ref-gates-evidence-only-2026-10-28, with STATUS superseded by remote-test-ref-gates-status-r9-2026-10-30. Keep remote gate acceptance separate from automatic typed credit.

5. Land under standing approval or actual acting-session permission; no repeated routine go. TermAl's integration owner performs the verified fast-forward/push/readback and exact-tree build/install under repository rules. The current OFF-evaluation exception is scoped to Opus2/session-8111: see greg-standing-word-off-eval-landings-2026-10-30 and the local autonomy rule. Do not extend it to Merger2. Record actual missing/refused evaluation, observation or credit once with its repair owner; never invent PASS, native credit or seal, change bindings or edit store/policy to obtain done. Use supported authorized exceptions; otherwise delivered/evaluationpending remains explicit. Default independent evaluation uses exact-tree/build native evidence, item-path changes stale old checks, and missing typed checks stay OPEN. Follow rules-commit-messages. Greg restarts TermAl; no agent host restart.

6. Fable2 owns queue, placement and operational recovery. Central Cargo requires its named resource GO; no duplicate full gate. Prepare private ui/node_modules, lockfile/tools and at least50GiB before launch. Never use another session's source root as a shell cwd. Respect frozen inputs and other gates' resource grants. For a carried run freeze the source, use the supported native result wait or coordinator notify, end the turn, and recover terminal metadata on wake. TermAl owns runs/logs/wakes; no stdout following, polling or extra operator loop. Use rules-waits-and-wakes for the exact dependency, wake owner and recovery. Before reports read available mail/results; otherwise state last observation/time. Preserve host-recording constraints until its result/refusal settles.

7. Claims grant no Git/filesystem authority. No impersonation, clock/store edits, cancellation/reopening or new work to bypass a foreign claim. Verify a handoff recipient's actual live project/workdir/tracker binding; rediscover recreated sessions. Unrelated handoffs may proceed only without changing an active gate's claim/root/input/attribution. Before publication reconcile withdrawals.

8. After merge AND closure, automatically clean handed worktrees/build output under greg-2026-10-28-remote-hosts-acceptance-and-worktree-cleanup; existing sweep w-65afd9cec452, no duplicate task or extra gate. Resolve absolute targets inside the repo, avoid link traversal, and verify no active claim/process/frozen use, unpublished work, unrecorded run or pending notice. Retain only for a concrete recorded active need with owner/end condition; remove when it ends. Use git worktree remove without force, branch -d only for published unused branches; never broad git clean or deletion of main/master. Remove .logs/.evidence only after all served tasks close and retention ends. Record removals/retention.

One editor per canonical rule: Merger2 edits this key. Replace stale wording, full-read verify, keep history in task notes; no second changing policy. Distinguish local full reads from quoted cross-project text. An inaccessible memory/result is an access gap, not permission.

Merger -> Architect3: only concrete collaboration failures needing rule/workflow correction, with evidence, impact and owner. Routine READY, queue, run, landing and repair results go to task/Fable2. Architect3 is no routine notify/result relay/recovery owner; Advisor relays Greg <-> coordinators and never executes. No compliance-status loop.
